status: V3 draft after v2 review; no pilot or full-bank approval

items.objective: Distinguish pump runtime from other equipment maintenance counters.
items.discriminatingFact: MACS describes typical vacuum pump oil-change intervals. Which operating record supports that schedule?
items.sourcePassageLocator: MACS January 2025, printed page 23, vacuum pump maintenance paragraph; Appendix C 4.1.1 and 7.3.3
items.change: Replaced cylinder retest date with calendar time since the same pump’s last oil change. No change to the keyed operating-hours distinction.

options.text: Days since the last pump oil change
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Uses elapsed calendar time as a proxy for pump workload.
options.validOtherCondition: Calendar time describes elapsed time since service; a manufacturer may specify its own schedule. No universal calendar interval is asserted.
options.whyStemExcludes: The cited typical schedule is based on pump operation, which can vary between days.
options.sourcePassageLocator: MACS January 2025, printed page 23, vacuum pump maintenance paragraph

options.text: Elapsed operating hours
options.support: MACS gives pump operating hours as a typical basis for vacuum-pump oil changes, with the pump’s own instructions controlling. Calendar days and vehicle counts are imperfect proxies for operating time. Refrigerant throughput instead concerns the recovery filter’s service interval.
options.sourcePassageLocator: MACS January 2025, printed page 23, vacuum pump maintenance paragraph; Appendix C 4.1.1 and 7.3.3

options.text: Mass processed by the recovery filter
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Confuses the machine filter counter with the pump service counter.
options.validOtherCondition: A desiccant filter tracks refrigerant processed before replacement.
options.whyStemExcludes: The component is the vacuum pump, not the refrigerant filter.
options.sourcePassageLocator: 40 CFR part 82 subpart B Appendix C 4.1.1

options.text: Number of vehicles charged that day
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Uses completed jobs as an informal workload measure.
options.validOtherCondition: Job count can describe shop activity, but is not the stated pump interval.
options.whyStemExcludes: Evacuation durations differ; the manual gives operating hours.
options.sourcePassageLocator: MACS January 2025, printed page 23, maintenance paragraph

items.objective: Separate material compatibility from cleaning performance and vehicle applicability.
items.discriminatingFact: What has a flushing compound demonstrated by meeting SAE J2670?
items.sourcePassageLocator: MACS January 2025, printed page 22, Flushing A/C Systems
items.change: Rebuilt alternatives around adjacent real procedures.

options.text: Suitability for an OEM flushing procedure
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Treats SAE conformity as vehicle-manufacturer authorization.
options.validOtherCondition: OEM service guidance determines whether its system may be flushed.
options.whyStemExcludes: MACS separates manufacturer reservations from J2670 compatibility.
options.sourcePassageLocator: MACS January 2025, printed page 22, opening and final flushing paragraphs

options.text: Removal of debris from condenser passages
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Reads a flushing-material standard as a cleaning-performance certification.
options.validOtherCondition: Cleaning effectiveness must be established for the component and process.
options.whyStemExcludes: MACS expressly says compatibility does not assure cleaning.
options.sourcePassageLocator: MACS January 2025, printed page 22, last flushing paragraph

options.text: Compatibility with A/C system materials
options.support: J2670 addresses stability and compatibility. It does not establish debris-removal performance, complete removal of residual solvent, or permission to flush a particular manufacturer’s system. Those are separate questions before using a flushing process.
options.sourcePassageLocator: MACS January 2025, printed page 22, Flushing A/C Systems

options.text: Removal of solvent during evacuation
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Assumes compatible solvent also evaporates completely under vacuum.
options.validOtherCondition: Residual solvent removal is a separate process concern.
options.whyStemExcludes: MACS warns that prolonged vacuum may leave solvent.
options.sourcePassageLocator: MACS January 2025, printed page 22, solvent boiling-point paragraph

items.objective: Interpret the pressure-clearing step in a named machine’s filter replacement sequence.
items.discriminatingFact: In Robinair 34788NI filter-replacement training, a valid code is entered. What must finish before the shutdown prompt?
items.sourcePassageLocator: Robinair SP01972025 VER 01, printed pages 28–29, Filter Maintenance and Replace the Filter steps 1–2 and 7
items.change: Corrected chronology: valid code entry precedes clearing; the acceptance/shutdown display follows clearing. Explicitly scoped to model-specific training.
items.existingBankOverlap: Compare frozen EQP-005 filter identity/reset. This targets clearing before opening, not filter identity; avoid duplicate maintenance-sequence questions on expansion.

options.text: Reaching the filter capacity limit
options.sourcePassageLocator: Robinair printed page 28, capacity warning and high-pressure warning
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Confuses the maintenance trigger with preparation to remove the component.
options.validOtherCondition: The capacity limit locks out further use and prompts filter replacement.
options.whyStemExcludes: Reaching the limit does not clear refrigerant from the filter.

options.text: Completing vacuum pump oil warming
options.sourcePassageLocator: Robinair printed page 29, step 7
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Remembers that filter replacement and pump oil service are linked and reverses their order.
options.validOtherCondition: Oil warming begins after installation and power restoration.
options.whyStemExcludes: The filter has not yet been removed or replaced.

options.text: Clearing refrigerant from the existing filter
options.sourcePassageLocator: Robinair SP01972025 VER 01, printed pages 28–29, Filter Maintenance and Replace the Filter steps 1–2 and 7
options.support: After valid code entry, this model clears the existing filter before displaying acceptance and prompting shutdown. Filter capacity is a maintenance trigger, not a requirement to postpone early replacement. Oil warming and the leak check follow installation. Waiting for the prompt allows the prescribed refrigerant-clearing stage to finish before the connection is opened.

options.text: Passing the internal pressure leak check
options.sourcePassageLocator: Robinair printed page 29, final paragraph; page 32 Leak Check
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Treats a satisfactory leak test as permission to open the existing filter.
options.validOtherCondition: A leak check follows replacement and pump maintenance.
options.whyStemExcludes: The prerequisite to opening is the clearing stage; the later test checks the assembled machine.

items.objective: Distinguish phase-change heat absorption from sensible heating and heat release in a liquid-contact exposure.
items.discriminatingFact: Liquid refrigerant boils on skin at nearly constant temperature. Which heat transfer accounts for the contact cooling?
items.sourcePassageLocator: Honeywell Solstice yf SDS v3.4, section 4 Skin contact; OpenStax College Physics 2e 14.3, opening phase-change narrative
items.change: Rejected unrelated exposure hazards. Narrowed to heat-transfer explanations for the same contact event. This remains foundational physical understanding, not a treatment question.

options.text: Heat absorbed as the liquid warms
options.sourcePassageLocator: OpenStax 14.3 opening paragraphs contrasting temperature change and phase change
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Applies the familiar rule that absorbed heat raises temperature to a boiling liquid.
options.validOtherCondition: A liquid absorbs sensible heat when its temperature rises.
options.whyStemExcludes: The stated refrigerant remains near constant temperature while boiling.

options.text: Heat released as vapor condenses
options.sourcePassageLocator: OpenStax 14.3 opening paragraphs, energy released during condensation
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Reverses the phase transition and heat direction when recalling refrigerant heat exchange.
options.validOtherCondition: Condensation releases heat.
options.whyStemExcludes: The observed liquid is boiling; the skin loses rather than receives that phase-change heat.

options.text: Heat released as the vapor cools
options.sourcePassageLocator: OpenStax 14.3 opening contrast with temperature change; Honeywell SDS section 4
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Focuses on cold refrigerant vapor but reverses the direction associated with its own cooling.
options.validOtherCondition: A cooling vapor releases sensible heat.
options.whyStemExcludes: The event is liquid boiling at nearly constant temperature, not vapor losing sensible heat.

options.text: Heat absorbed as the liquid vaporizes
options.sourcePassageLocator: Honeywell Solstice yf SDS v3.4, section 4 Skin contact; OpenStax College Physics 2e 14.3, opening phase-change narrative
options.support: Vaporization takes energy from the surroundings, including contacted skin, even without a rise in refrigerant temperature. Warming a liquid requires a temperature rise. Condensation and vapor cooling release heat rather than accounting for heat removed from the skin. Rapid liquid evaporation is the frostbite mechanism identified by the refrigerant SDS.

items.objective: Distinguish the verification procedure authorized by 82.40(f) from retraining, recertification and substitution of another demonstrator.
items.discriminatingFact: EPA investigates a certified technician’s recovery practices. Which verification procedure is authorized by Section 82.40(f)?
items.change: Removed the live-act versus three-paperwork partition. All alternatives now describe verification or training procedures involving a person performing a task.

options.text: Retake the certification test through its issuer
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Equates an enforcement check of current technique with repeating the certification examination.
options.validOtherCondition: Certification testing and recertification are addressed separately; revocation requires recertification before further service.
options.whyStemExcludes: The question concerns the on-site demonstration provision for a presently certified technician.

options.text: Operate recovery equipment at the business premises
options.support: Section 82.40(f) permits EPA to require the technician’s own demonstration at the business premises. It does not specify a substitute demonstration by the owner, repeat training, or an automatic certification retest for this verification. Separate recertification provisions apply in their own circumstances, including after revocation.

options.text: Repeat practical training with the course provider
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Treats referral to an instructor as the required way to verify practical competence.
options.validOtherCondition: Instructor-led or on-the-job training is an approved means of training.
options.whyStemExcludes: The specified provision authorizes direct demonstration at the business premises.

options.text: Have the shop owner demonstrate for the technician
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Assumes the owner can demonstrate the business’s competence on an employee’s behalf.
options.validOtherCondition: The owner could demonstrate their own competence if they were the technician being checked.
options.whyStemExcludes: The inquiry concerns the named technician’s ability, not another operator’s ability.

items.objective: Resolve a concrete equipment acquisition against the common-owner and establishment-operator requirements.
items.discriminatingFact: Rae operates the garage and owns its recover-only machine; Lee owns the off-site recycler. Which arrangement permits recycling there?
items.change: Replaced remote ownership actors with four plausible transactions between the same two parties. The stem’s operator and ownership roles determine which transaction qualifies.
items.existingBankOverlap: Consolidate with frozen REG-025. These are the same legal ownership objective, not additional coverage.

options.text: Lee buys Rae’s recovery machine
options.sourcePassageLocator: 40 CFR 82.32(e)(2); hypothetical ownership facts in stem
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Checks ownership of both machines but overlooks who operates the extraction establishment.
options.validOtherCondition: This acquisition could satisfy the relationship if Lee also owned or operated the extraction establishment.
options.whyStemExcludes: The stated operator is Rae; Lee only owns the off-site recycler.

options.text: Rae leases Lee’s recycling machine
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Treats possession or exclusive access to the second machine as ownership.
options.validOtherCondition: Leasing supplies access to equipment, but is not the ownership specified by this exception.
options.whyStemExcludes: The clause requires the same person to own both machines.

options.text: Rae buys Lee’s recycling machine
options.support: Rae already operates the extraction establishment and owns the recovery machine. Buying Lee’s recycler gives Rae ownership of both machines, satisfying the off-site recycling ownership condition. Lee buying the recovery machine leaves the common equipment owner separate from the garage operator. Leasing or contracting access does not establish the required ownership. Reclamation is a separate route.

options.text: Rae contracts recycling work to Lee
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Assumes a commercial recycling contract can substitute for the ownership chain.
options.validOtherCondition: A separate reclamation arrangement is possible; contracting ordinary recycling alone does not meet this exception.
options.whyStemExcludes: Lee would remain the separate owner of the recycler.

items.objective: Choose the moisture-control intervention for prolonged atmospheric exposure.
items.discriminatingFact: An A/C circuit remained uncapped throughout prolonged collision repairs. Which measure best addresses the resulting moisture problem?
items.sourcePassageLocator: MACS January 2025, printed pages 23–24, evacuation and Desiccant Failure
items.change: Moved the exposure condition into the stem; alternatives are actual, distinct contamination-control procedures.

options.text: Replace the system desiccant
options.sourcePassageLocator: MACS January 2025, printed pages 23–24, evacuation and Desiccant Failure
options.support: Prolonged atmospheric exposure can saturate system desiccant, so MACS recommends replacing it. Evacuation removes air and vapor but does not reliably resolve this moisture condition. Pump oil service maintains pump performance; recycling cleans recovered refrigerant outside the vehicle, not saturated desiccant remaining inside it.

options.text: Extend the evacuation period
options.sourcePassageLocator: MACS January 2025, printed pages 23–24, evacuation discussion
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Extrapolates the role of evacuation in moisture removal to saturated desiccant.
options.validOtherCondition: Adequate evacuation is needed before recharging and may require time for the entire circuit to reach deep vacuum.
options.whyStemExcludes: Page 24 specifically warns that even good evacuation may not remove this moisture and recommends desiccant replacement.

options.text: Change the vacuum pump oil
options.sourcePassageLocator: MACS January 2025, printed page 23, vacuum pump maintenance
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Attributes poor moisture removal to degraded vacuum-pump performance.
options.validOtherCondition: Pump oil changes maintain evacuation performance at the manufacturer’s interval.
options.whyStemExcludes: The stated cause is prolonged vehicle-circuit exposure, not overdue pump maintenance.

options.text: Recycle the recovered refrigerant
options.sourcePassageLocator: 40 CFR 82.32(e)(1); MACS January 2025, printed page 24
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Assumes cleaning the recovered fluid also restores the vehicle’s moisture-control component.
options.validOtherCondition: Recovered refrigerant must be properly processed before reuse.
options.whyStemExcludes: External refrigerant processing does not replace saturated desiccant inside the exposed circuit.

items.objective: Distinguish both end use and service scope in the top-off-only purchase exception.
items.discriminatingFact: Which business receives an equipment exception under federal MVAC servicing requirements?
items.sourcePassageLocator: 40 CFR 82.32(e)(4); EPA Section 608 and Section 609 Overlap, MVAC-like appliances
items.change: Removed top-off-only from the stem so both service scope and appliance class must be assessed. Options and explanation unchanged.
items.existingBankOverlap: REG-007 MVAC-like certification is a different obligation; review together to avoid teaching identical category recognition repeatedly.

options.text: Business opening off-road cab systems for repair
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Applies the MVAC-like exception to any work on that equipment.
options.validOtherCondition: Charging alone qualifies for the exception.
options.whyStemExcludes: Opening the circuit is broader than top-off-only work.

options.text: Business limited to passenger-car refrigerant top-offs
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Applies the limited-work exception to every vehicle type.
options.validOtherCondition: Top-offs of MVAC-like appliances qualify.
options.whyStemExcludes: Passenger-car systems are MVACs, for which purchase is expressly required.

options.text: Business opening passenger-car systems for repair
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Assumes equipment is required only when refrigerant is resold.
options.validOtherCondition: Servicing a refrigerant circuit requires properly using approved equipment.
options.whyStemExcludes: Passenger-car circuit repair meets neither part of the exception.

options.text: Business limited to off-road cab refrigerant top-offs
options.support: Section 82.32(e)(4) exempts facilities that only charge MVAC-like appliances from purchasing recycling equipment, while retaining technician certification. Passenger-car top-offs require equipment purchase. Opening MVAC-like systems requires approved equipment to be available, and passenger-car repairs require approved equipment use.

items.objective: Separate current-job oil removal from prior-job residue.
items.discriminatingFact: A collection bottle held 8 mL before recovery and 20 mL afterward. How much fresh oil replaces this removal?
items.sourcePassageLocator: MACS January 2025, printed page 16, oil recovery reservoir caption
items.change: Explanation only: removed the unsupported assumption that the initial oil came from another job.
items.existingBankOverlap: SRV-002 simple oil replacement quantity overlaps; consolidate into this accounting decision before expansion.

options.text: 8 mL
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Uses the starting mark as the job’s removal.
options.validOtherCondition: 8 mL is the recorded quantity already present.
options.whyStemExcludes: It predates the current recovery.
options.sourcePassageLocator: MACS January 2025, printed page 16 reservoir caption; arithmetic from stem

options.text: 28 mL
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Adds the starting amount to the final reading rather than subtracting.
options.validOtherCondition: Addition would combine two separate job quantities, not cumulative readings.
options.whyStemExcludes: The final mark already includes the starting oil.
options.sourcePassageLocator: MACS January 2025, printed page 16 reservoir caption; arithmetic from stem

options.text: 20 mL
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Assumes the bottle was empty and uses its final reading.
options.validOtherCondition: Final reading measures this job when the bottle starts empty.
options.whyStemExcludes: The stem gives an 8 mL starting balance.
options.sourcePassageLocator: MACS January 2025, printed page 16 reservoir caption; arithmetic from stem

options.text: 12 mL
options.support: This job added 20 minus 8, or 12 mL, to the bottle. Replace that removed quantity with fresh oil of the required type. The 8 mL was already present; 20 mL includes that pre-existing quantity, and 28 mL double-counts the starting quantity. Emptying the bottle beforehand prevents this error.
options.sourcePassageLocator: MACS January 2025, printed page 16, oil recovery reservoir caption

items.objective: Identify the actual defect in a proposed purchaser declaration, rather than reconstruct a checklist from options.
items.discriminatingFact: Written statement: buyer name, business address, “resale or shop use.” For small CFC-12 cans, what correction enables the exception?
items.change: Replaced majority-component reconstruction with a supplied declaration and four actual corrective actions. Only one correction addresses the supplied defect.
items.existingBankOverlap: Related to REG-018 and REG-020 purchaser routes, but this is document defect identification. Review the cluster before any expansion.

options.text: State and follow resale-only intent
options.support: The statement already identifies the purchaser, includes its business address and is written. Its defect is the proposed shop use. For the under-20-pound CFC-12 resale exception, the purchase must be solely for resale, and the written statement must accurately reflect that intent. Changing words while retaining shop use would not qualify.

options.text: Supply the purchaser’s business address
options.sourcePassageLocator: 40 CFR 82.42(b)(3); hypothetical statement in stem
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Recognizes the address requirement but fails to check the supplied declaration.
options.validOtherCondition: A declaration omitting the purchaser’s business address needs that information.
options.whyStemExcludes: The stem already supplies the business address.

options.text: Identify the purchaser instead of the supplier
options.sourcePassageLocator: 40 CFR 82.42(b)(3); hypothetical statement in stem
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Anticipates a common invoice-header identity error.
options.validOtherCondition: A statement giving only the supplier’s identity must identify the purchaser instead.
options.whyStemExcludes: The supplied declaration gives the buyer’s own name.

options.text: Provide the declaration in writing
options.sourcePassageLocator: 40 CFR 82.42(b)(3); hypothetical statement in stem
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Remembers that an oral assurance does not satisfy this record requirement.
options.validOtherCondition: An oral resale assurance must be documented in writing.
options.whyStemExcludes: The stem explicitly supplies a written statement.

items.objective: Distinguish vapor distribution from vapor generation and ignition properties.
items.discriminatingFact: Which R-1234yf property explains why ventilation must address a service pit as well as the workbench?
items.sourcePassageLocator: Honeywell Solstice yf SDS sections 5–6 and 9; MACS January 2025, printed page 43 precaution 1A
items.change: Rebuilt alternatives around adjacent real procedures.

options.text: Vapor is denser than surrounding air
options.support: Vapor density greater than air allows released refrigerant to accumulate in low areas. Evaporation creates vapor, pressure depends on temperature, and flammability affects ignition risk; those facts do not explain its tendency to collect in a pit.
options.sourcePassageLocator: Honeywell Solstice yf SDS sections 5–6 and 9; MACS January 2025, printed page 43 precaution 1A

options.text: Vapor can ignite within a concentration range
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Connects pit ventilation only to the A2L fire warning.
options.validOtherCondition: Concentration affects ignition possibility.
options.whyStemExcludes: Flammability does not explain why vapor accumulates low.
options.sourcePassageLocator: Honeywell SDS section 9; MACS January 2025, printed page 44

options.text: Vapor pressure increases with temperature
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Uses a familiar refrigerant pressure-temperature relationship to explain release behavior.
options.validOtherCondition: Temperature affects pressure in a containing system.
options.whyStemExcludes: The question asks about vertical accumulation after release.
options.sourcePassageLocator: Honeywell SDS section 9 vapor pressure

options.text: Liquid evaporates readily after release
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Recognizes that spilled refrigerant becomes vapor and attributes location to evaporation.
options.validOtherCondition: Ready evaporation explains the production of vapor.
options.whyStemExcludes: It does not distinguish a pit from an elevated location.
options.sourcePassageLocator: Honeywell SDS section 6

items.objective: Distinguish allowed machine actions after a failed pressurized check from earlier and later sequence stages.
items.discriminatingFact: R-1234yf passes vacuum decay but leaks during the partial-charge check. Which operation remains permitted?
items.sourcePassageLocator: MACS January 2025, printed page 51, R-1234yf recharge sequence
items.change: Rebuilt alternatives around adjacent real procedures.

options.text: Delivering the remainder of the programmed charge
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Treats the successful vacuum test as sufficient authorization to finish.
options.validOtherCondition: The balance is charged after both checks pass.
options.whyStemExcludes: The pressurized check found a leak.
options.sourcePassageLocator: MACS January 2025, printed page 51, second paragraph

options.text: Repeating the initial 15% charging step
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Treats the small test dose as a repeatable diagnostic top-up.
options.validOtherCondition: The initial 15% is added after the vacuum test passes and the detector is positioned.
options.whyStemExcludes: That stage has already occurred and failed.
options.sourcePassageLocator: MACS January 2025, printed page 51, final sequence paragraphs

options.text: Injecting replacement compressor lubricant
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Treats oil replacement as independent of the failed refrigerant check.
options.validOtherCondition: Fresh replacement oil is required to replace oil removed during recovery, following the equipment procedure.
options.whyStemExcludes: The described lockout allows only recovery and re-evacuation.
options.sourcePassageLocator: MACS January 2025, printed page 16, oil replacement; page 51, lockout paragraph

options.text: Beginning recovery of the test charge
options.support: After a leak is detected during the pressurized check, the described machine permits recovery or re-evacuation. The balance requires passing both checks. Adding the test dose belongs to an earlier stage, and lubricant replacement is not an exception to the lockout.
options.sourcePassageLocator: MACS January 2025, printed page 51, R-1234yf recharge sequence

items.objective: Match charge information to the installed component and its revision.
items.discriminatingFact: Condenser C205 revision B replaces C101. Which hypothetical record supplies the applicable charge specification?
items.sourcePassageLocator: MACS January 2025, printed page 25, service revisions and replacement condenser instructions; original hypothetical record data
items.change: Replaced predeclared obsolete references with neutral records carrying component and revision identifiers. No refrigerant quantity or real technical bulletin was invented.

options.text: VIN label: C101 original assembly
options.sourcePassageLocator: MACS page 25; hypothetical record identity supplied in option
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Gives the vehicle-linked label priority without checking the component change.
options.validOtherCondition: The VIN label can govern the original C101 assembly.
options.whyStemExcludes: C101 has been replaced by C205 revision B.

options.text: Installation sheet: C205 revision B
options.sourcePassageLocator: MACS January 2025, printed page 25, service revisions and replacement condenser instructions; original hypothetical record data
options.support: The installation sheet matches both the installed C205 component and revision B. The VIN label and workshop table describe C101, while the bulletin concerns C205 revision A. These are hypothetical records illustrating applicability, not real manufacturer part numbers or bulletins. The lesson is to match current instructions to the installed configuration, not to rank document types universally.

options.text: Service bulletin: C205 revision A
options.sourcePassageLocator: MACS page 25, late component changes and revised charge instructions; hypothetical revision facts
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Recognizes the matching part number but overlooks the revision difference.
options.validOtherCondition: A bulletin for C205 revision A applies when that revision is installed.
options.whyStemExcludes: The stem identifies revision B.

options.text: Workshop table: C101 original assembly
options.sourcePassageLocator: MACS page 25; hypothetical configuration facts
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Uses the model-level workshop capacity without checking the installed assembly.
options.validOtherCondition: The workshop table can govern the C101 assembly it describes.
options.whyStemExcludes: The installed assembly is C205 revision B.

items.objective: Apply the salvage-specific processing route rather than a universal purchaser claim.
items.discriminatingFact: Unreclaimed salvage MVAC refrigerant is being reused. Which facility must perform the required recycling?
items.change: Rejected broad exclusive-buyer claim. Replaced with the explicit unreclaimed salvage processing route.
items.existingBankOverlap: Review REG-025 off-site common ownership and REG-005 generic reuse: salvage-specific facility condition is distinct, but explanations must preserve scope.

options.text: Facility charging it into the receiving vehicle
options.support: For this salvage reuse route, Section 82.34(d)(1)(ii)(B) assigns recycling to the facility that charges or recharges the refrigerant. Recovery at the salvage yard is an earlier step. Off-site reclamation is a separate route; an independent recycler is not substituted for the recharging facility in this provision.

options.text: Salvage facility that extracted it from the donor
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Assumes the original recovering facility must also do the cleaning.
options.validOtherCondition: The disposal facility may recover with dedicated approved equipment.
options.whyStemExcludes: The recycling obligation is assigned to the facility doing the recharge.

options.text: Reclamation facility receiving it for purification
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Confuses the two permitted salvage processing routes.
options.validOtherCondition: A reclamation facility can process refrigerant under the alternative reclamation route.
options.whyStemExcludes: The question specifies unreclaimed refrigerant reused through recycling.

options.text: Independent MVAC recycler hired by the seller
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Applies an outsourced recycling arrangement to the salvage reuse route.
options.validOtherCondition: Off-site recycling has a separate, limited common-ownership provision in 82.32(e)(2).
options.whyStemExcludes: This salvage provision specifically requires recycling by the recharging facility.
